footer.notMedicalAdviceText: SaafSaans is an urban environmental planning tool. See a doctor if you experience breathlessness, chest pain, or wheezing that does not settle.
footer.googleAttribution: Map and place search powered by Google Maps Platform. Air quality data from Google Air Quality API.

swaps.shift-outdoor-exercise: Move outdoor exercise to the cleanest window when particulate levels are lowest.
swaps.exercise-indoors: Move strenuous workouts indoors to reduce inhaled particle dose during dirty hours.
swaps.shut-windows-peak: Keep windows closed during morning and evening pollution spikes to slow infiltration.
swaps.air-house-clean-window: Ventilate your home during the afternoon when outdoor air is cleanest.
swaps.purifier-bedroom: Run an air purifier in the bedroom overnight to protect sleeping family members.
swaps.diy-fan-filter: Use a fan with a high-efficiency filter as an affordable clean air setup.
swaps.mask-outdoors: Wear a well-fitted mask during travel or outdoor activity to filter particulate matter.
swaps.no-mosquito-coil: Switch to mosquito nets or plug-in repellents to remove a heavy indoor smoke source.
swaps.incense-outside: Light incense near open windows or outdoors to avoid high indoor particle levels.
swaps.cook-with-exhaust: Use an exhaust fan and lids while cooking or frying to clear indoor fumes.
swaps.wet-mop: Wet-mop floors instead of dry sweeping to trap settled dust without stirring it up.
swaps.metro-not-car: Take the metro instead of driving to reduce personal exposure and street emissions.
swaps.bus-not-car: Take the city bus instead of driving to reduce personal road emissions.
swaps.carpool: Share rides with colleagues to divide vehicle fuel use and emissions.
swaps.walk-short-trips: Walk or cycle short local trips during cleaner hours instead of driving.
swaps.wfh-day: Work from home one day each week to skip commute emissions and road exposure.
swaps.no-idling: Turn off vehicle engines at long traffic signals to cut avoidable exhaust.
swaps.no-burning: Avoid burning dry leaves or garden waste, and report open fires to authorities.

facts.mosquitoCoil: Burning one mosquito coil releases as much PM2.5 as burning 75 to 137 cigarettes.
facts.incense: In one test house, burning incense raised indoor PM2.5 to 197 µg/m³.
facts.frying: Frying without a stove hood reached a median 4.5 mg/m³ of PM2.5, against 0.5 mg/m³ with the hood on.

advice.wetMop: Wet-mop floors instead of dry sweeping to remove dust without resuspending particles.
advice.diyFanFilter: A box fan taped to a high-efficiency filter can serve as a low-cost filter setup.
advice.noIdling: Turn off vehicle engines at long traffic signals to cut avoidable exhaust.
advice.noBurning: Avoid burning dry leaves or garden waste, and report open fires to authorities.

summary.default: Personalised air quality actions for your household routines and local forecast.

cpcb.Satisfactory: May cause minor breathing discomfort to sensitive people.
cpcb.Moderately polluted: May cause breathing discomfort to people with lung disease such as asthma, and discomfort to people with heart disease, children and older adults.
cpcb.Poor: May cause breathing discomfort to people on prolonged exposure, and discomfort to people with heart disease
cpcb.Very Poor: May cause respiratory illness to the people on prolonged exposure. Effect may be more pronounced in people with lung and heart diseases.
cpcb.Severe: May cause respiratory effects even on healthy people and serious health impacts on people with lung/heart diseases. The health impacts may be experienced even during light physical activity

why.sensitivity: Asthma, heart conditions and pregnancy make dirty air harder on the body.
why.routine: Where someone spends the day decides the air they breathe.
why.exercise: Breathing hard outdoors takes in the most air.
why.exerciseTime: So we can compare it with the cleanest hours.
why.mode: Each way of travelling puts out a different amount of CO₂.
why.distance: Longer trips save more when you switch.
why.days: How many days a week the trip happens.
why.sharing: Sharing a vehicle splits its CO₂ between people.
why.area: A bigger room needs a bigger purifier.
why.height: High ceilings mean more air to clean.
why.windows: Open windows let more outdoor air in.
why.cooking: Frying without a hood fills the kitchen with smoke.
why.purifier: So we do not suggest one you already have.
why.cadr: With it we can check your purifier is big enough. Leave empty if you do not know.
why.incense: Incense raises the smoke indoors a lot.
why.coils: One coil gives off as much smoke as many cigarettes.
why.destination: So Google Maps can measure your trip; we only use it to fill in the distance.

aqi.body: The Air Quality Index turns the main pollutants into one number on India's CPCB scale, from zero to five hundred. Higher is worse. Each range has a name, from Good to Severe.

pm25.body: Tiny particles in the air, thinner than a hair, that reach deep into the lungs. They come from vehicles, dust, smoke and cooking. We measure them in micrograms in each cubic metre of air (µg/m³).

dose.body: How much {pm} a person breathes in over the day: how dirty the air is where they are, how fast they breathe for their age and activity, and for how long. Breathing harder outdoors adds up fastest.

cigarettes.body: A rough comparison from Berkeley Earth: breathing air with a day's average of twenty two µg/m³ of {pm} is about as harmful as smoking one cigarette. It compares health risk, not smoke.

cadr.body: Clean Air Delivery Rate: how much clean air a purifier gives out, in cubic feet a minute (cfm). The bigger the room, the higher the CADR it needs. Look for it on the box.

estimate.body: Some values are picked from inside a published range, such as how fast particles settle indoors, or come from an operator's own claim, such as the metro saving. We label those numbers Estimate.
